summary: Cygnus Logistics - peak tokenization timeouts causing streaming stalls and request backlog (post-incident follow-up)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported sustained request timeouts and streaming stalls during their nightly bulk shipment tokenization job (batch window 02:00-03:30 ET). A subset of requests experienced tokenization timeouts at the serving-runtime layer which cascaded into streaming stalls and client-side disconnects. Impact: ~18% of Cygnus production requests in the window returned 504/timeout and ~12% stream sessions closed without final chunk, impacting order confirmations and downstream workflows.

Impact:
- Customer reported order processing delays and duplicate background retries triggered by the client after streaming stalls.
- Temporary spike in token and request counts due to retries produced a billing exposure; Cygnus flagged for credit review.

Environment:
- prod, us-east-1, customer using enterprise account with pinned model redwood-open-3b and quantized variant for cost-sensitive routes.

Steps to reproduce (observed in-incident):
1) Customer submits parallelized batch tokenization job (500k short prompts) using streaming chat API with allow_partial=true.
2) Backend pressure on KV cache eviction increases due to skewed prefix distribution.
3) Tokenization workers fall back to slower kernel path for quantized model leading to high tail latency and internal timeouts.
4) Streaming connection resets observed in ~20s window after initial tokenization delay.

Relevant logs / signals:
- Serving-runtime trace IDs: sr:20260310:us-e-0a:trace:* (attached to incident folder).
- Autoscaler events: repeated scale-up/scale-down cycles between 02:12 and 02:36 (spike in instance churn).
- KV cache evictions increased 12x baseline; miss rate grew from 3% -> 35%.
- Router returned 504s with message "tokenizer_timeout" and streaming disconnects with ECONNRESET logged at edge.

Customer quote (initial):
"Large batches started failing mid-window. Streaming stopped giving final chunk and our retry logic duplicated jobs. We need assurance this won't happen at scale."
comments: 2026-03-10 02:28 - Maya Chen (Support): Initial report received via priority channel. Customer experiencing streaming stalls and timeouts during nightly run. Escalated to SRE and on-call infra.

2026-03-10 02:45 - Elena Gomez (SRE): Acknowledged incident. Triage: observed rising KV eviction rate and kernel fallback path triggering long tail latencies. Opening incident bridge (#inc-cygnus-20260310).

2026-03-10 03:10 - Ravi Patel (Runtime Eng): Noted a recent kernel-selection rollout at 01:40 that changed quantized model fallback thresholds. Rolling back kernel selection flags to prior safe defaults as hotfix. Monitoring for improvement.

2026-03-10 03:28 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer confirmed streaming success rate improving after rollback. Some clients still reported retries and duplicate side-effects. Initiated billing review and temporary credits offered.

2026-03-11 09:15 - Elena Gomez (SRE): Post-incident data collection completed. Root cause hypothesis documented. Preparing follow-ups and action items. Shared interim postmortem draft to customer-linked Confluence.
2026-03-13 11:02 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer accepted initial remediation and asked for concrete rollout plan for kernel-selection guards and autoscaler smoothing.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Kernel selection rollout (PR #1187) aggressively shifts quantized runs to new fast path without accounting for skewed prefix distributions; when prefix cache misses spike, execution falls back to a slower kernel inducing tokenization timeouts.

Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler reacts to increased per-instance CPU/memory by rapidly scaling up, but scale-down was triggered too aggressively when latency briefly improved, causing cold-start pressure and additional cache churn.

Data points: KV cache miss rate rose to 35% and TTL evictions increased. Correlated traces show tokenization step timeouts aligning with misses. The rollback at 03:00 reduced timeouts to baseline within 10 minutes.

Customer behavior: large parallel batch submitted with high prefix similarity causing hot keys and poor cache locality; allow_partial=true meant clients retried on timeout leading to duplicate downstream requests and billing spike.
Reproducibility: Synthetic test with same batch profile reproduced elevated tail latency when kernel-selection flag enabled; reproducer located in infra/tests/issue-240999-runbook.
Related items: linked INT-412 (autoscaler smoothing investigation) and SUP-70012 (previously similar failover pattern for dedicated capacity under quantized fallback).
resolution: Hotfix: Rolled back the kernel-selection thresholds (PR revert of serving-runtime PR #1187) and applied a temporary increased KV cache allocation for Cygnus' route to reduce evictions. Autoscaler policy adjusted to increase scale-down cooldown from 30s to 5m to avoid thrash. Customer received immediate mitigation; error rates returned to baseline by 03:20. Billing team approved a retroactive credit to cover duplicated jobs and retry-induced token counts. Incident bridge closed once success rate stabilized.
follow_up_actions: ENG-1221 (Runtime): Implement safe-guard for kernel-selection that rejects fast-path when KV miss-rate > 15% (owner: Ravi Patel) - target 2026-03-27
OPS-909 (Autoscaler): Add hysteresis and longer cooldown windows for scale-down during high-variance workloads; create canary for 48-hour monitoring (owner: Priya Nambiar) - target 2026-03-20
DX-77 (Docs/SDK): Update guidance for customers on large parallelized batch patterns: recommend prefix sharding and client-side jitter to avoid hot-keying (owner: Nadia Wallace) - target 2026-03-19
SRE-archive: Add Cygnus reproducer to incident runbooks and include telemetry dashboard with KV miss-rate + kernel path breakdown (owner: Elena Gomez) - target 2026-03-17
Finance: Finalize customer credit amount and close billing dispute (owner: Carla Ruiz) - target 2026-03-15
postincident_summary: This incident was triggered by an aggressive kernel-selection rollout that did not account for a pathological request distribution from the customer's parallel tokenization job. The immediate rollback and cache allocation prevented further user-visible impact. Long-term mitigations include kernel-selection guards, autoscaler hysteresis, and customer-facing guidance to avoid hot-keying. All high-priority follow-ups assigned with owners and due dates. Customer expresses measured satisfaction with the response and accepted the credit offer.
billing_impact: Estimated duplicate-token exposure: ~650k tokens billed during incident window. Finance approved provisional credit; final reconciliation pending.
